findings.claim: the February 2018 'Beast from the East' was 'dumping more than 50 cm of snow in parts of Cumbria'
findings.truth: The deepest snow of the 2018 cold wave was 57 cm in Gloucestershire; Storm Emma gave up to 50 cm on southern uplands. Cumbria was not among the worst-hit areas, which were eastern and southern Britain.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, 2018 Great Britain and Ireland cold wave (max snowfall 57 cm, Gloucestershire)

findings.claim: “November 2010’s anticyclone trapped −19°C readings in Scotland for over a fortnight”
findings.truth: The severe blocked spell peaked in December 2010 - the coldest UK December in the Met Office record - with −21.2°C at Altnaharra on 2 December. The lesson's own conclusion and mark scheme already say December 2010, so the content contradicted them.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Winter of 2010-11 in Great Britain and Ireland

findings.claim: Storm Desmond “flood[ed] more than 5,000 homes in Carlisle” (repeated in KC 4 and in two mark schemes)
findings.truth: About 5,200 homes were flooded across Cumbria and Lancashire in total; Carlisle itself had roughly 2,200 properties flooded. The 5,000 figure is the regional total, not the Carlisle total.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Storm Desmond ('About 5,200 homes were flooded in Lancashire and Cumbria')

findings.claim: “four people killed in the UK during Eunice” / “four UK deaths”
findings.truth: Storm Eunice killed three people in the UK; the fourth death commonly reported alongside them was in the Republic of Ireland.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Storm Eunice (three fatalities in the United Kingdom)

findings.claim: a micro-climate “can differ from the regional climate by several degrees in temperature and several seconds in wind speed”
findings.truth: Wind speed is measured in metres per second (or knots / mph), never in seconds.
findings.evidence: unit error, self-evident

findings.claim: “London is the safest urban heat island choice for Eduqas.”
findings.truth: House rule: an Eduqas/WJEC lesson must never name the board in student-facing prose.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings

findings.claim: mark scheme evidences western Scotland with “Seathwaite over 3,300 mm/yr”
findings.truth: Seathwaite is in Cumbria, England, so it cannot support a statement about western Scotland. The western Highlands do exceed 3,000 mm a year.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Seathwaite, Allerdale; Met Office UK rainfall averages

findings.claim: “Why is Seathwaite in Cumbria the wettest place in the UK?”
findings.truth: Seathwaite is the wettest INHABITED place, at about 3,552 mm a year. Nearby Sty Head Tarn takes about 4,369 mm, and Crib Goch in Snowdonia more still.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Seathwaite, Allerdale

findings.claim: “Eduqas requires students to know one small-scale UK ecosystem.”
findings.truth: House rule: never name the board in student-facing prose. The spec requirement itself (5.3.2, one located small-scale UK ecosystem) is correct.
findings.evidence: spec 5.3.2; CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings

findings.claim: “Eduqas asks students to study one tropical biome…” and “a balance Eduqas explicitly tests”
findings.truth: House rule: never name the board in student-facing prose. The underlying scope claim matches spec 5.4.2 (rainforest plus one contrasting biome).
findings.evidence: spec 5.4.2; CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings

findings.claim: Belo Monte “drowned 668 km² of forest and indigenous land to power 60 million homes”
findings.truth: Belo Monte's installed capacity is 11,233 MW with a low load factor; it cannot supply 60 million homes. The developer's claim, widely quoted, is enough electricity for about 60 million PEOPLE.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Belo Monte Dam (11,233 MW, completed Nov 2019); arithmetic on household demand

findings.claim: the Swansea Bay tidal lagoon “was rejected in 2018 partly on cost, partly on ecological grounds”
findings.truth: The UK government refused the scheme in June 2018 purely on value for money - it judged the cost to consumers and taxpayers far higher than alternative low-carbon power. Ecological objections existed but were not the stated reason.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Swansea Bay Tidal Lagoon (government value-for-money statement)

findings.claim: “In the UK … only 14% of rivers in ‘good’ ecological status (Environment Agency, 2020)”
findings.truth: The Environment Agency regulates England only; the 14% figure is for English rivers. Scotland (SEPA) and Wales (NRW) publish their own, much higher, figures.
findings.evidence: Environment Agency remit; the same fix was made in the sibling landscapes unit (F11 there)

findings.claim: “Eduqas examiners particularly reward links between the impact … and the wider system”
findings.truth: Fabricated examiner claim, and it names the board. No examiner report is quoted or quotable here.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md - fabricated examiner claims are FIX

findings.claim: “Eduqas requires students to know one rainforest example …” and “Eduqas requires the same biome to be used …”
findings.truth: House rule: never name the board in student-facing prose. Both scope claims match spec 5.4.3.
findings.evidence: spec 5.4.3; CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned strings

findings.claim: “National Parks (Brazil’s 422 protected areas)”
findings.truth: No published Brazilian count of 422 exists. Brazil has 76 national parks; its federal conservation units number about 334.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, List of national parks of Brazil

findings.claim: “Compare with Brazil’s Chamå tribal reserves: indigenous land rights have been shown by the World Bank to slow deforestation by up to 50% compared with adjacent unprotected forest.”
findings.truth: There is no Brazilian indigenous territory called 'Chamå' - the name (with a stray a-ring) is fabricated, and the specific World Bank 50% figure is not traceable. The general finding that Brazilian indigenous territories hold deforestation far below neighbouring unprotected forest is well supported.
findings.evidence: no source for the named reserve or the figure; the fabricated character å is itself a tell

findings.claim: “one of the highest tourism revenues per visitor in Latin America — over US$3.4 billion in 2019” and “ecotourism revenue exceeded US$3.4 billion in 2019”
findings.truth: Costa Rica took US$4.01 billion in international tourism receipts in 2019 from 3.139 million visitors. US$3.4 billion understates it, the figure is a national total rather than a per-visitor rate, and it is all tourism rather than ecotourism alone.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Tourism in Costa Rica (2019: 3.139m visitors, US$4.010bn)

findings.claim: “the FSC now certifies more than 200 million hectares globally” (and the same figure in the KC matching option)
findings.truth: FSC-certified forest area is about 160 million hectares and has never exceeded 200 million; it was 165 million hectares in 2012 and fell after Russian certificates were suspended in 2022.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Forest Stewardship Council (165 million ha, September 2012)

findings.claim: “For 8-mark evaluate questions, examiners reward judgement”
findings.truth: Fabricated examiner claim. The advice itself is sound; the attribution is not.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md - fabricated examiner claims are FIX

findings.claim: “By 2024, more than 200,000 hectares were under community-managed conservancies, supporting around 25% of Kenya’s wildlife… Local Maasai now earn over US$8 million a year in lease payments.”
findings.truth: None of the three numbers could be verified from Wikipedia or an official source in this session. The Maasai Mara Wildlife Conservancies Association publishes lower figures (roughly 24 conservancies over about 160,000 ha, with lease payments nearer US$5 million a year), and the '25% of Kenya's wildlife' claim normally attaches to the whole greater Mara ecosystem, not to the conservancies. Options: (a) re-source all three from MMWCA and correct them, (b) drop the three numbers and keep the qualitative case, or (c) leave as is pending a source.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Maasai Mara has no conservancy figures; MMWCA site not fetched (WebSearch budget exhausted)

findings.claim: hedgerows “support pollinators that fertilise nearby crops — about £500m worth of crop pollination every year in the UK”, and a flashcard asks which hedgerow service is “worth around £500m per year”
findings.truth: Published UK valuations of insect pollination to crops run about £400m-£690m a year and cover ALL pollinators in ALL habitats, not hedgerows alone. £500m sits inside that range but the attribution to hedgerows is not supported. Recommend re-wording to 'insect pollination is worth hundreds of millions of pounds a year to UK crops, and hedgerows shelter many of those pollinators' rather than correcting the number.
findings.evidence: no single settled UK figure; range from POST / UK NEA valuations

findings.claim: “Costa Rica gets around 60% of its tourists for nature-based holidays”
findings.truth: The Costa Rican Tourism Board's published figure is that 47% of international tourists took part in ecotourism activities (2009). 60% is repeated in textbooks but has no traceable source. Recommend softening to 'about half' unless a current ICT figure can be found.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Tourism in Costa Rica (ICT, 47% in 2009)

findings.claim: Belo Monte “drowned 668 km²”
findings.truth: Wikipedia gives a combined reservoir surface of about 441 km² (108 + 333). 668 km² is the total flooded area quoted by campaign groups for the original scheme. Not settled enough to correct.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Belo Monte Dam

findings.claim: Storm Eunice had “a central pressure of 969 mb”
findings.truth: Not confirmed by any source reachable this session; Met Office reporting puts the minimum near 970 hPa, so the figure is plausible. The 196 km/h gust at The Needles and the England record are both confirmed.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Storm Eunice (gust and record confirmed; pressure absent)

findings.claim: “insured losses estimated at £500m for Desmond”
findings.truth: Wikipedia puts total damage at at least £870m and gives no insured/uninsured split; the ABI's £1.3bn covers Desmond, Eva and Frank together. £500m matches early PwC insured-loss estimates for Desmond alone, so it is defensible.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Storm Desmond

findings.claim: “rainfall in the southern Amazon has fallen by around 25% since 1970”
findings.truth: The published finding of that size concerns DRY-SEASON rainfall in the southern Amazon since about 1979, not annual rainfall since 1970. The direction and rough size are right; the framing overstates.
findings.evidence: climatological literature on southern Amazon dry-season rainfall

findings.claim: African elephants “have fallen from 12 million in 1900 to around 415,000 today”
findings.truth: 415,000 is the IUCN African Elephant Status Report figure and is sound. The 12 million for 1900 is widely repeated but rests on no census; other common figures are 3-5 million for the 1930s-40s.
findings.evidence: IUCN African Elephant Status Report 2016

findings.claim: Costa Rica protects “nearly 25%” of its territory and forest cover is “60% today”
findings.truth: Published protection is 23.4% - 'nearly 25%' is within tolerance. Forest cover is 57.1% on the national figure and about 60% on FAO's FRA 2020, so 60% is defensible. No edit.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Tourism in Costa Rica; FAO FRA 2020

summary: Scope and paper structure check out against Core Theme 5 and the Component 2 assessment description, and the 1/2/3/4/6/8-mark ladder matches the rest of the Eduqas geography fleet. Twenty FIX findings: seven board-naming or fabricated-examiner breaches, and thirteen wrong or invented figures - the worst being a fabricated Brazilian 'Chamå' reserve, Belo Monte 'powering 60 million homes', and Storm Desmond's 5,200 Cumbria-and-Lancashire flood total presented as 5,000+ homes in Carlisle alone.
